Alright, let me think about this year...

---

I'm 42, been farming these 2.6 mu since I got married into this village. My husband works construction in town most of the year, so the field is mostly my responsibility, plus my mother-in-law helps some when she can. The two kids are in school, so they're not much help except weekends and summer.

With only 2.6 mu, we're not making rich off this land — most of our cash income comes from my husband's work. But the grain from these fields feeds us and the pigs, and whatever maize we don't use we can sell. So I manage it carefully. I can't afford to waste money on inputs, but I also can't afford a bad harvest — we count on that grain.

**Wheat first.** I planted the winter wheat back in October like I always do, around the 10th. Used Jimai 22 variety — it's what most people around here plant, I bought a bag of certified seed from the agro-supply store in town, about 15 kg for my 2.6 mu. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, about 40 kg per mu as base fertilizer. That's what the extension guy recommended a few years back and it works fine for me. I rotary tilled the field after the maize came off, then sowed with the village's shared seeder.

Now it's spring, wheat is greening up. I'll irrigate once at green-up in early March — water from the tube well costs money, the electricity adds up, so I try not to overdo it. At that first irrigation I'll topdress with urea, about 15 kg per mu. Then another irrigation at jointing around late April, and one more before grain filling if it hasn't rained enough. My neighbor Aunt Wang only irrigates twice and she still gets decent yield, but I've had problems with late frost damage when the field is dry, so I like to keep it moist.

For weeds I'll spray a herbicide in spring — the little packets from the agro store, mixed in the sprayer. Last year I saw some aphids at heading so if I see them again I'll do one insecticide spray. I'm hoping for about 450 kg/mu this year — last year was 440, the year before 470, so somewhere in that range.

**Then maize right after.** This is the tight part. Wheat harvest combine comes around June 8-10, and I need to get maize in within a few days. I hire the combine driver from the village — he charges about 60 yuan/mu — then I use the no-till planter service another neighbor offers, another 25 yuan/mu. The maize seed is Zhengdan 958 or whatever hybrid the shop has in — I buy a bag every year, can't save hybrid seed. About 2 kg per mu. I put compound fertilizer in with the seed, another 30-35 kg per mu of the 15-15-15.

Maize is rain-fed mostly here in summer — it's the rainy season. But if July gets dry I'll irrigate once or twice. I topdress urea at knee-high stage, maybe 15 kg per mu. If I see armyworm or corn borer I'll spray. Harvest in late September, I usually get around 500 kg/mu.

Total input cost is what worries me most — I try to keep it under about 450 yuan per mu per crop. That's already a big chunk of cash out the door before we see any grain.

decision.reasoning_summary: With only 2.6 mu and my husband working off-farm, I keep things close to what's worked for me the past few years — compound fertilizer as base plus one urea topdress on each crop, three irrigations on wheat and one on maize in a normal-rain year. I don't chase the highest yield because every extra bag of fertilizer or extra irrigation is cash out of my pocket, but I also don't cut corners on seed or skip the topdress because losing yield would hurt us more. I hire the combine and no-till planter because there's no way I'm getting maize in on time by hand, and the cost is worth it.
